small_guidance:
- The current gather kernel iterates kh*kw*ceil(IC/BLOCK_K) tl.dot calls with BLOCK_K=32/64 and IC=64 — that's tiny K per dot. Increase BLOCK_K to 64 (full IC in one shot) and drop the inner IC loop entirely; also try BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=128 with num_warps=8, num_stages=2 as the primary config.
- Most (h_in, w_in) combinations are invalid because of the stride==2 modulus check — the entire tl.dot still runs with zeros. Hoist the stride-modulus test outside the dot by indexing on h_out%STRIDE / w_out%STRIDE so each program only visits the (kh, kw) pairs that match its phase (KH/STRIDE * KW/STRIDE = 4 iterations instead of 16).
- Switch the output store to write contiguous (N, H_out, W_out, OC) tiles (channels-last out) or transpose offs_n to the inner contiguous dim so the store coalesces; currently offs_n strides by H_out*W_out which is non-coalesced.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a scatter-add ConvTranspose: one program per (N, IC tile, H_in tile, W_in tile), load the input tile and the full (OC, KH, KW) weight slice, compute the input×weight outer product, and atomically (or via deterministic accumulation into a per-program output region with no overlap because stride==KH/2 means kernels do overlap — use atomics or split by kh%stride, kw%stride phase). This matches the natural data flow of transposed conv and avoids the modulus-gated gather where 3/4 of the work is wasted.
- Alternatively, since stride==2 and kernel==4 partition cleanly, implement as 4 separate "phase" GEMMs: for each (ph, pw) in {0,1}×{0,1}, the output pixels with (h_out%2, w_out%2)==(ph,pw) are produced by a dense GEMM of shape (N*H_in*W_in, OC) with K=IC*(KH/2)*(KW/2)=IC*4. This eliminates all masking inside the dot and turns the problem into 4 clean GEMMs of K=256, which Triton handles very well.
- Use channels-last (NHWC) layout for both input and output so the IC and OC axes are contiguous; this lets the GEMM-K and GEMM-N loads coalesce and removes the strided output store that currently bottlenecks the kernel.
